nodes.label: ADR-0022: apps/web feature folders — pages route, features own the capability
nodes.rationale: One-folder-per-route let app/login/page.tsx reach 388 lines with a state machine, four sub-components, timers and transport error handling in one file, because nothing capped page size. It also scattered one capability (auth spans login, signup, onboarding) across route folders that can share nothing.

nodes.label: apps/web/features/<feature>/ owns screens, components, hooks, CSS
nodes.rationale: app/ is Next.js routing only. A capability's files change together and now live together — auth's three screens share features/auth/shared/ without a satellite that belongs to no route. lib/ is unchanged as app-wide infrastructure.

nodes.label: page.tsx is a ≤50-line controller
nodes.rationale: Reads route params, calls one controller hook, renders one screen component; a reader follows two files instead of one, accepted as the same trade the container/presentational split already makes.

nodes.label: Biome noExcessiveLinesPerFunction (maxLines 50) on app/**/page.tsx
nodes.rationale: A lint rule rather than a line-counting script is a standing owner preference: it measures the function BODY so imports and comments do not eat the budget, and it is versioned with the toolchain. This is what stops the shape degrading silently the way the previous convention did.

nodes.label: Amendment: barrels at two levels, never mixing server and client
nodes.rationale: A barrel re-exporting both a Server Component and a 'use client' screen attaches the client chunk to every page reaching it, and no tree-shaking removes it — that cost /design 147 kB against a 102 kB baseline until GalleryScreen moved to features/design-reference/gallery/.

nodes.label: package.json sideEffects: ["**/*.css"]
nodes.rationale: A bare import './x.css' is a side effect, so without the declaration webpack keeps every module a barrel names — all three auth routes shipped an identical 183 kB. True of this app today and must be rechecked if that stops being the case.

nodes.label: A feature is named for the API module that owns it
nodes.rationale: Keeps Law 6 traceability intact and makes 'where does this go?' answerable without judgement.

nodes.label: Amendment: the asymmetry is LOCATION, not structure
nodes.rationale: Inside the folder both platforms use the same split (screen composes · components/ one file each · hooks/use-<thing>.ts · styles beside them). Reading the ADR as licence for a single-file RN screen produced a 446-line LoginScreen against web's 70; structural parity is what lets a reviewer diff the platforms file-for-file.

nodes.label: apps/mobile deliberately NOT changed (src/screens/<name>/)
nodes.rationale: RN has no router-driven app/ directory, so src/screens is already the equivalent shape; recorded in both CLAUDE.md files so a later agent does not 'align' one to the other.

nodes.label: Rejected: keep route folders, add a line cap
nodes.rationale: Caps the symptom, leaves auth scattered across three route folders with nowhere shared for use-online.ts.

nodes.label: Rejected: src/features/ next to app/
nodes.rationale: A sibling features/ under apps/web is one fewer level and matches how lib/ already sits.

nodes.label: Rejected: feature-per-route (features/login, features/signup)
nodes.rationale: Reproduces the scattering this ADR exists to remove — auth's three screens share state shape and copy.

hyperedges.label: Mechanical gates chosen over prose to stop silent degradation
